I have identified the issue in `rich/segment.py` within the `Segment._split_cells` method, which relates to incorrect boundary handling when splitting a segment at a specific cell position. The fix involves changing the condition from checking for exact equality (`cell_pos == cut`) to checking if the accumulated cell length meets or exceeds the cut position (`cell_pos >= cut`). This ensures that the split is performed correctly even if the character width calculation causes a slight overshoot. The code compiles successfully after the change.

I am submitting the patch now.
